customManagers.description: Surface new Camel K runtime releases by watching the version recorded in the quarkus-camelk comment block. This never auto-merges: the matching packageRule holds it behind Dependency Dashboard approval, because bumping this line alone would make the comment describe a platform combination no operator actually reports.

packageRules.description: Front the anonymous Maven Central endpoint with Google's full CDN mirror. Mend-hosted Renovate shares a source-IP pool that Sonatype (repo.maven.apache.org, Cloudflare-fronted) now 429s under load; a 429 on a POM with no warm Redis entry raises an external-host-error, which aborts the whole repository run before the lookup/PR phase - so no PRs and no Dependency Dashboard updates. The GCS bucket is a byte-for-byte mirror of Central with no rate limit; keep Central as the fallback so anything the mirror lags on still resolves.

Never look up CamelBee's own published artifacts. They are released from this repo, so a 'new release' is always something this build just pushed - bumping them here is meaningless and every coordinate costs a maven-metadata.xml + POM fetch on each run, inflating the request burst that trips the Central rate limiter.

The Camel K flavour pins the platform the Camel K runtime actually ships (read off the operator's camelcatalog). These two BOMs must not be bumped to catch up with the sibling quarkus BOM - see the comment in dependencies/quarkus-camelk/pom.xml. The core-only-quarkus-sample example pins the same floor for the same reason (see its own comment). Test-only deps in dependencies/quarkus-camelk/pom.xml are still updated.

One Camel version per CamelBee release, set by the Quarkus platform. Quarkus cannot take a Camel release before Camel Quarkus ships it and the platform picks it up (2-5 weeks after a Camel release), so Spring Boot (camel-spring-boot-bom), standalone (camel.version), camel-maven-plugin and shared-core (shared.camel.version, which must never be ahead of Quarkus or a newer-only API fails there with NoSuchMethodError) are all held at the camel-core version that quarkus-camel-bom pins for quarkus.platform.version. New Camel releases show up on the Dependency Dashboard only. Do not tick them on their own: when a quarkus.platform.version PR brings a newer Camel (check camel-api in quarkus-camel-bom-<version>.pom), move all four to that exact version in the same change. Decided 2026-11-13 after 4.23.0 split the runtimes (Spring Boot/standalone 4.23.0, Quarkus 4.22.1). Does not touch org.apache.camel.quarkus (Camel K rule) or the core-only-* floor samples (examples/ is ignored by config:recommended).
packageRules.groupName: Camel (held to the Quarkus platform's Camel)

packageRules.description: Surefire, failsafe and the report plugin are held at 3.5.6. 3.6.0's console-output capture (StackWalkerStrategy) loads a class through Quarkus's FacadeClassLoader while the main thread holds its lock waiting on the deployment-dependency resolver; a JDK/JUL log line from a resolver thread then deadlocks the forked test JVM forever (seen in security/quarkus-security, 2026-09-25). Grouped so the three can't drift. Lift the cap only after a fixed surefire/Quarkus release, verified by repeated full 'mvn clean install' runs.

Byte Buddy publishes every release twice: the normal build (1.18.17) and a legacy Java 5 build with a -jdk5 suffix (1.18.17-jdk5). Maven Central's metadata lists the -jdk5 build as 'latest', so Renovate proposed it (2026-11-11). Ignore -jdk5 versions; only the normal build is wanted.

jacoco-maven-plugin must match the org.jacoco version the io.quarkus:quarkus-jacoco extension bundles (0.8.15 on Quarkus 3.40.1.2). quarkus-jacoco records @QuarkusTest coverage with its own jacoco runtime into target/jacoco.exec; when the plugin's report/check runs a newer jacoco, that data is silently dropped. With 0.8.16, security/quarkus-security fell from ~91% to 19% line coverage (every @QuarkusTest-exercised class at 0 lines) and failed the 0.80 gate, though all tests passed (2026-11-11). Affects security/quarkus-security and starters/camelbee-quarkus-starter. Raise the cap only together with a quarkus.platform.version bump whose quarkus-jacoco pulls the newer org.jacoco (check with 'mvn dependency:tree -pl security/quarkus-security -Dincludes=org.jacoco').

Avro is capped below 1.12.2 on purpose. 1.12.2 added org.apache.avro.util.ClassSecurityValidator to ClassUtils.forName, which SpecificDatumReader.setSchema reaches via SpecificData.getClass. Its default trust list is JDK scalars only, so camel-avro's data format throws SecurityException on every generated record class ('Forbidden <pkg>.Order! This class is not trusted to be included in Avro schemas'). Archetype scenario 9 caught it: all 28 springboot avro variants failed while quarkus passed on 1.12.1 from the platform BOM. 1.12.1 is the only version with both the Utf8.compareSequences the generated code needs (1.12.0, which apicurio-registry-serdes-avro-serde pulls transitively, lacks it) and no validator. Lifting this cap is not a renovate.json edit: adopting 1.12.2+ means setting org.apache.avro.SERIALIZABLE_CLASSES / SERIALIZABLE_PACKAGES in every generated microservice before the data format initialises. The runtime and the codegen plugin are grouped so they can never drift apart - dependencies/springboot/pom.xml requires avro.version to match avro-maven-plugin.version.
packageRules.groupName: Avro (runtime + codegen plugin, must move together)

packageRules.description: Quarkus langchain4j-bom must equal the langchain4j-core version quarkus-camel-bom pins (1.19.3 on platform 3.39.5). Ahead of it, every Quarkus LANGCHAIN4JAGENT/EMBEDDING project dies at boot with NoClassDefFoundError dev/langchain4j/internal/ProviderJsonSpec. Lift the cap only together with a quarkus.platform.version bump whose bom pins the newer langchain4j-core.

Notify only. A new camel-k-runtime release appears as an unchecked box on the Dependency Dashboard and creates no branch or PR until someone ticks it. Ticking it is not the fix: re-read a live operator with 'kubectl get camelcatalog -o jsonpath={.items[0].spec.runtime.metadata}' and update the comment block AND quarkus.version / camel-quarkus.version together in one hand-written PR.
packageRules.commitMessageTopic: Camel K runtime (re-pin quarkus-camelk BOMs by hand)
